Candidate-distribution sensitivity is distinct from popularity bias: sampled metrics can change model rankings without changing model parameters. Frequency-matching negatives to positives does not establish unbiased evaluation; candidate sampling interacts with popularity and missing observations. Thus, a frequency-matched diagnostic alone cannot identify the cause of poor HR@10. [Candidate Set Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11723); [On Sampled Metrics](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2021/0651.pdf).

Direct GRU4Rec evidence supports changing sampling jointly with an appropriate loss. Hidasi and Karatzoglou show that averaging BPR/TOP1 over many easy negatives dilutes gradients; simply increasing negative count can hurt. Their controlled experiments compare negative counts, popularity exponents and losses: cross-entropy favors popularity sampling with small pools, more uniform sampling with large pools; ranking-max losses favor intermediate exponents. Additional sampling plus improved losses produced gains up to approximately 35% over earlier GRU4Rec results, with diminishing returns around 2,048 extra negatives in one dataset. These are session-based Recall/MRR@20 results, not guaranteed Amazon HR@10 gains. [GRU4Rec study](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf).

Proposed distinguishing controls: keep official candidates/evaluator fixed; inspect validation accuracy within target-frequency bins, score–frequency association within bins, and repeat-target versus novel-target performance. Compare intact versus shuffled histories to test sequence dependence; inspect training/validation curves and gradient norms to distinguish memorization from incomplete optimization. These are diagnostic proposals, not findings about the current model. A concrete next experiment: retain one GRU4Rec per category, fix negative count and all training settings, and compare uniform sampling against q(i) ∝ training_frequency(i)^0.5 using the same loss; subsequently compare cross-entropy against regularized BPR-max with the sampler fixed. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10, preserving seed 42 and training limits.
